mapping_basis: The paper names DNb08, a MANC type name in type_list.csv mapping to exactly one type; driver_lines.csv also lists SS70620 as DNb08.
notes: Adjudicated from abstract only: bioRxiv full text returned HTTP 429 on all attempts, Nature redirected to login, Europe PMC preprint PPR1083778 has no full text. Only line_specificity was disputed; preparation/effector/stimulation copied from the experiment-defining columns of disagreements.csv; headless_surface set to 'other' because the surface could not be read. Abstract says rhythmic leg movements but not which legs, so per-leg fields are 'unclear'; non-disputed fields from the original readers (who read full text) should take precedence. Abstract contains a simulation driver call for DNb08.
quote: a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies.
source_locator: Abstract (Europe PMC MED:42951971); experiment per disagreements row: bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.12.675944v2 Fig. 5c-e, Supplementary Video 2 (not opened: bioRxiv HTTP 429)
stimulation: 638 nm LED laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at body-coxa joint of front left leg; 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly (as given in the disagreements row; not verified by adjudicator)
title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
